social.title: Cancún FC Under the Lights
social.description: Second-division fútbol at the Andrés Quintana Roo — cheap seats, loud drums, and the city's actual sporting heart.
social.bonus: Buy the scarf. Wear the scarf.

social.title: Dinner Show Chaos at Pericos
social.description: Forty years of sombreros, conga lines, and tequila carts — Cancún's most gleefully over-the-top cantina show on Avenida Yaxchilán.
social.bonus: Volunteer for whatever the waiters are recruiting for.

social.title: Fiesta Barge Night at Xoximilco
social.description: Cancún's answer to the trajineras — a floating dinner party down torch-lit canals with mariachi, cumbia, and tequila passed boat to boat.
social.bonus: Join the singing by song two, not song ten.

social.title: Litros and Botanas at La Chopería
social.description: The downtown beer hall where litre mugs, football on every screen, and free botanas keep whole tables of cancunenses planted for hours.
social.bonus: Order the michelada preparada and commit to it.

social.title: Salsa Till Late at Grand Mambo Café
social.description: Cancún's great live-orchestra salsa hall — locals dressed to kill, bands from Havana, and a floor that does not care if you're new.
social.bonus: Take the free intro lesson, then use it immediately.

social.title: Sunset Catamaran Party to Isla Mujeres
social.description: The booze cruise to Isla Mujeres is unashamedly touristy and completely irresistible — open bar, Caribbean sunset, strangers who become your best friends for exactly four hours.
social.bonus: Jump off the boat at the snorkel stop last — make it a moment, not a splash.

social.title: Sunday Market at Mercado 23
social.description: Mercado 23 is the oldest working market in Cancún — a chaotic, color-saturated maze of spice vendors, fresh tortilla stalls, and grandmothers who've been selling the same salsa for thirty years.
social.bonus: Buy one ingredient you don't recognize and ask the vendor what to do with it.

social.title: Bar Crawl Through Avenida Yaxchilán
social.description: Cancún's local nightlife strip in El Centro has none of the tourist theater of the Hotel Zone and all of the actual fun — cantinas, mezcalerías, and live norteño.
social.bonus: Order whatever the person next to you is drinking at every stop — no questions asked.

social.title: Rooftop Pre-Party at Coco Bongo Terrace
social.description: Before the main show swallows you whole, the Coco Bongo terrace bar is where the city's nightlife really ignites — cheap drinks, city views, and no cover before midnight.
social.bonus: Strike up a conversation with someone from a country you've never met anyone from before.

social.title: Rooftop Drinks at Nomads Hostel Sky Bar
social.description: This Downtown rooftop bar draws a sharp mix of long-term travelers and local twenty-somethings for cheap mezcal, loud playlists, and a city skyline view no hotel pool can match.
social.bonus: Buy a round for the table next to you and join them for the rest of the night.

social.title: Saturday Night at Parque Las Palapas
social.description: Downtown Cancún's central plaza fills every weekend with local families, food vendors, cumbia blasting from competing speakers, and zero tourists — this is the real city.
social.bonus: Join a strangers' table, buy a round of elotes, and stay until you've learned at least one person's name and job.

foodie.title: Aguachile Verde at Los Aguachiles
foodie.description: The Riviera's favourite marisco counter does shrimp three shades of green-hot on tostadas that never stop coming.
foodie.bonus: Order the spiciest aguachile and finish it without bread.

foodie.title: Ceviche Conga at El Cejas, Mercado 28
foodie.description: The market's legendary marisquería where waiters break into conga lines between delivering towers of ceviche — lunch as floor show.
foodie.bonus: Join the conga line when it forms. Not if. When.

foodie.title: Midnight Burrito at The Surfin Burrito
foodie.description: A 24-hour surf-shack counter in the Hotel Zone where the burritos are named after breaks and the 3am line is half bartenders getting off shift.
foodie.bonus: Go after midnight — that's when it's itself.

foodie.title: Lunch at the Cocinas of Mercado 28
foodie.description: Past the souvenir maze, the market's open-air cocinas serve sopa de lima and poc chuc to the people who actually live here.
foodie.bonus: Eat where the taxi drivers are eating.

foodie.title: Seafood Lunch at El Fish Fritanga
foodie.description: A locals' fritanga hidden mid-Hotel-Zone — plastic chairs, lagoon breeze, and aguachile that embarrasses the resort buffets uphill.
foodie.bonus: Ask what came off the boat this morning and order that.

foodie.title: Fish Tacos at Los de Pescado
foodie.description: Baja-style battered fish tacos done the Cancún way at the local chain that out-cooks every beach club at a fifth of the price.
foodie.bonus: Dress it from every salsa on the bar exactly once.

foodie.title: Marquesitas After Dark at Parque de las Palapas
foodie.description: The crepe-crisp marquesita — Nutella, cheese, both — was born on the peninsula and the stands ringing Las Palapas make the definitive ones.
foodie.bonus: Order the classic: queso de bola WITH Nutella. Trust it.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Tempo by Martín Berasategui
foodie.description: The only Michelin-recognized kitchen in Cancún channels Basque precision into Caribbean ingredients — this is the meal that reframes everything you ate before it.
foodie.bonus: Introduce yourself to the sommelier and ask them to pair every course with a different Mexican wine — no imported bottles.

foodie.title: Dinner at Restaurante La Parrilla
foodie.description: A Cancún fixture since the 1970s, La Parrilla grills mesquite-fired meats tableside and pours strong margaritas while mariachi bands work the room with zero irony.
foodie.bonus: Request the mariachi play a song you don't know and learn the chorus by the second verse.

foodie.title: Ceviche Lunch at La Habichuela Downtown
foodie.description: Open since 1977, this garden-courtyard institution serves Yucatecan seafood and cocobichuela cocktails in a setting that feels like old Cancún never left.
foodie.bonus: Ask the waiter to recommend a dish that's not on the English menu — then order it without hesitation.

foodie.title: Seafood Tostadas at El Pescado Ciego
foodie.description: Downtown Cancún's best-kept ceviche counter serves cold shrimp, octopus, and fish tostadas stacked to structural failure for the price of a hotel minibar water.
foodie.bonus: Order one of everything on the menu — if it comes to under 200 pesos you're obligated to tip 30%.

chill.title: Take the Last Ferry Back from Isla Mujeres
chill.description: The day-trippers leave by five — stay for the lights coming up across the bay and ride the near-empty ferry home.
chill.bonus: Ride the open top deck no matter the wind.

chill.title: Coffee Crawl on Avenida Nader
chill.description: The leafy avenue behind Avenida Tulum is downtown's café row — specialty roasters, patio tables, and the Cancún that lives here year-round.
chill.bonus: Two cafés minimum; rank them out loud.

chill.title: Hammock Hour at Playa Chac-Mool
chill.description: Playa Chac-Mool sits mid-Hotel Zone but draws a calmer local crowd than the resort beaches, with natural shade palms, gentler surf, and beach vendors selling cold coconuts instead of shot trays.
chill.bonus: Buy a coconut from a beach vendor and ask them to chop it with a machete tableside — then tip them well.

chill.title: See MUSA from a Glass-Bottom Boat
chill.description: The underwater museum without getting wet — five hundred silent statues slipping past under glass.
chill.bonus: Pick one statue and find out its story afterward.

chill.title: Golf-Cart Loop of Isla Mujeres to Punta Sur
chill.description: Ferry over, rent a cart, and putter the island's one road to the sculpture-strewn cliffs of Punta Sur — the easternmost point of Mexico.
chill.bonus: Be standing at Punta Sur when the ferry crowds are still at brunch.

chill.title: Sunset Walk on the Malecón Tajamar
chill.description: Downtown's lagoon-front boardwalk faces west over Nichupté — runners, families, and the day ending in orange behind the mangroves.
chill.bonus: Spot a crocodile eye from a safe, dry distance.

chill.title: Morning Swim at Playa Langosta
chill.description: The Hotel Zone's calmest public bay — bath-warm, wave-free, and nearly empty before ten.
chill.bonus: Float on your back until you lose count of the minutes.

chill.title: Afternoon in Parque de las Américas
chill.description: This grand Art Deco park in El Centro has been the city's civic heart since the 1940s — fountains, shade trees, chess tables, and no tourist in sight.
chill.bonus: Challenge one of the chess regulars to a game — if you lose in under ten moves, you buy them a paleta.

chill.title: Dawn Watch at Punta Cancún Lookout
chill.description: The rocky point where the Hotel Zone curves north offers an unobstructed view of the Caribbean turning from black to violet to blinding gold — and you'll almost always have it alone.
chill.bonus: Arrive before the sun and stay without taking a single photograph — just watch.

chill.title: Afternoon at Museo Maya de Cancún
chill.description: The finest archaeological museum on the Mexican Caribbean houses 400 pre-Columbian pieces in a sleek modern building that's cool, calm, and almost always half-empty.
chill.bonus: Find the piece with the oldest date marker and spend ten full minutes with just that one object.

chill.title: Read on the Quiet End of Playa Gaviota Azul
chill.description: The western stretch of this Hotel Zone beach stays uncrowded well into midday — white sand, turquoise water, and the kind of silence that makes a book feel like a luxury.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in your bag for the entire visit — no photos, no checking, nothing.

chill.title: Hammock Float at Playa Norte, Isla Mujeres
chill.description: The waist-deep water off Isla Mujeres' north beach is the calmest, clearest, most absurdly turquoise paddling pool in the Caribbean, and the hammocks strung over it make time stop.
chill.bonus: Stay in your hammock until you've watched at least three complete strangers walk past knee-deep with their phones held overhead — appreciate that you aren't them.

chill.title: Sunset Watch from Playa Delfines
chill.description: The westward-facing end of the Hotel Zone's finest public beach turns molten at dusk, and the concrete Cancún sign here has become the city's unofficial town square at golden hour.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in your bag for the entire golden hour — no photos, just the actual sunset.

active.title: Morning Loop of Parque Kabah
active.description: Downtown's pocket of preserved jungle has a shaded running loop where coatis cross the path like they own it — because they do.
active.bonus: Full loop without stopping; coati sightings are free points.

active.title: Cenote Kantun-Chi Snorkel and Cave Walk
active.description: An hour south of Cancún, Kantun-Chi is a family of four connected cenotes — open sky, semi-cave, and full cave — where you can snorkel and walk through stalactite chambers that have been open to visitors for over 30 years.
active.bonus: Float face-down in the darkest chamber of the cave cenote for 60 seconds — don't move, don't splash, just listen to the absolute silence.

active.title: Deep-Sea Fishing out of Puerto Juárez
active.description: Charter a panga from the working docks at Puerto Juárez and head into open Caribbean water for mahi-mahi, sailfish, and wahoo with crews who fish these waters every single day.
active.bonus: If you catch something, negotiate with the captain to take it to a nearby restaurant and have it cooked — most will play along.

active.title: Snorkel Puerto Morelos Reef National Park
active.description: One of the most protected and therefore healthiest reef sections on the entire Mesoamerican Barrier Reef lives just offshore in shallow, crystal-clear water.
active.bonus: Count at least ten species before surfacing — moray, parrotfish, and barracuda are on the board.

active.title: Zip-Line Over Selvatica Cenote Circuit
active.description: Selvatica's jungle circuit strings together twelve zip-lines, ATVs, and a cenote plunge into one relentlessly fun half-day that earns every peso.
active.bonus: Take the final zip-line hands-free — both arms out, no gripping the harness straps.

active.title: Paddleboard Sunrise at Playa Tortugas
active.description: Rent a board before the beach crowds arrive and you get the entire glassy lagoon-side channel to yourself as the sun clears the horizon.
active.bonus: Hold a tree pose on the board for a full 30 seconds without falling in.

active.title: Cenote Azul Day Trip
active.description: This open-air cenote on the Riviera Maya road is one of the most beautiful natural swimming holes near Cancún and somehow still uncrowded by noon.
active.bonus: Jump from the highest platform on your first try — no working up to it.

active.title: Snorkel Punta Nizuc Reef
active.description: The southernmost tip of the Hotel Zone hides a living coral reef you can reach straight from the beach, no boat required.
active.bonus: Find and photograph a sea turtle — no points if it's a photo of someone else's turtle.

active.title: Bike the Hotel Zone to Punta Nizuc
active.description: The dedicated bike lane running the full 14-kilometer spine of the Hotel Zone south to Punta Nizuc is the fastest and most honest way to read the city from end to end.
active.bonus: Stop at every public beach access point along the route — touch the water at each one before moving on.

active.title: Run the Hotel Zone Coastal Path at Sunrise
active.description: The 14-kilometer stretch of Boulevard Kukulcán between Playa Tortugas and Playa Delfines runs directly along the Caribbean and is best experienced at 6am when it belongs entirely to you.
active.bonus: Run the full 14km without stopping for a single photo — save the view for the turnaround point.

adventure.title: Drive the Ruta de los Cenotes
adventure.description: From Puerto Morelos a jungle road strings together a dozen swimmable cenotes — pick two, swim both, and let the day disappear.
adventure.bonus: Choose one cenote by name alone and don't look it up first.

adventure.title: Walk the Quiet Ruins of El Meco
adventure.description: North of the ferry docks sits a small Maya site with a climbable-view pyramid, iguanas everywhere, and almost nobody else.
adventure.bonus: Count the iguanas — first to twenty wins.

adventure.title: Spend the Day at Ventura Park
adventure.description: Cancún's amusement park stacks waterslides, a wave pool, ziplines, and go-karts at the far tip of the Hotel Zone.
adventure.bonus: Ride the biggest slide first, before you can talk yourself out of it.

adventure.title: Boat Out to the Bird Island of Isla Contoy
adventure.description: Only two hundred visitors a day are allowed on this national-park island of frigatebirds and empty white sand — the Caribbean before anyone built anything.
adventure.bonus: Count frigatebirds until you give up.

adventure.title: Beat the Buses Into Chichén Itzá at Opening
adventure.description: Arrive at the gates the moment they open at 8am and you'll walk the site in near-total silence before the tour buses arrive and ruin everything.
adventure.bonus: Stand at the base of El Castillo and clap once — listen for the quetzal echo that bounces back.

adventure.title: Wakeboard at Aquaworld Cancún
adventure.description: Aquaworld has operated on Laguna Nichupté for decades and their wakeboard boats deliver the flattest, fastest water in the zone with instructors who don't let you quit.
adventure.bonus: Attempt a surface 180 turn — you won't stick it but you have to try at least twice.

adventure.title: Swim with Whale Sharks from Cancún
adventure.description: From June through September, the world's largest fish congregate in the waters north of Holbox, and jumping into the water beside one is categorically life-rearranging.
adventure.bonus: Match the whale shark's pace and swim alongside it for a full 60 seconds without grabbing the guide's arm.

adventure.title: Jet Ski the Open Caribbean from Playa Tortugas
adventure.description: Renting a jet ski from Playa Tortugas and punching out past the reef line into true open water is the Hotel Zone's most unapologetically reckless good time.
adventure.bonus: Cut the throttle in deep water, slide off the ski, and float face-down in the open Caribbean for one full minute.

adventure.title: Explore Ruinas del Rey Archaeological Zone
adventure.description: A genuine pre-Columbian temple complex sits buried inside the Hotel Zone itself, surrounded by iguanas the size of cats and almost zero tourists.
adventure.bonus: Find the largest iguana on site and sit close enough that it doesn't move — bonus if it climbs on you.

adventure.title: Parasail over the Hotel Zone
adventure.description: Three hundred feet up over the turquoise gradient between Cancún's lagoon and open Caribbean is the only view that makes sense of this city's layout.
adventure.bonus: Go tandem with a stranger you just met on the beach — introduce yourself only after you're airborne.

adventure.title: Kayak the Mangroves of Nichupté
adventure.description: You push a kayak into the brackish channels behind the Hotel Zone and enter a cathedral of red mangrove roots that swallows the resort noise completely.
adventure.bonus: Kill your paddle and drift in complete silence for two full minutes — no talking, no phone.

adventure.title: Swim the Cenote Dos Ojos Cave System
adventure.description: One of the Yucatán's most awe-inducing flooded cave networks sits 90 minutes from Cancún and rewards with cathedral light shafts and zero-visibility black zones.
adventure.bonus: Enter the Bat Cave section with your snorkel and swim the full dark passage without turning back.

adventure.title: Kiteboard Laguna Nichupté
adventure.description: The Hotel Zone's massive lagoon is one of the flattest, most consistent kiteboarding flats in Mexico, and lessons here will have you riding by day two.
adventure.bonus: Signal your instructor you're ready to drop the training bar and ride unassisted — do it before the session ends.

adventure.title: Zipline Over the Reef at Garrafón Park
adventure.description: Isla Mujeres' cliffside park strings its zipline out over turquoise reef water — the Caribbean under your feet at full speed.
adventure.bonus: Jump from the highest accessible ledge on your first attempt — no standing around deliberating.

adventure.title: Snorkel the MUSA Underwater Museum
adventure.description: You drift above 500 life-sized submerged sculptures colonized by coral and fish in the Cancún lagoon, and it reads like a fever dream gallery opening.
adventure.bonus: Touch nothing, photograph everything — find the 'Silent Evolution' group and count how many sculptures have coral growing from their eyes.
